title: Blending CVC words
examples: How do I know when I have blended all the sounds?
Can we try blending longer words next time?
What does CVC stand for again?

explain.say: Listen carefully to the sounds I say for you. I will say the sounds one by one.
Now we will push those sounds together very fast. Say /c/ /a/ /t/ blended together.
When we push the sounds together we make a word. Like this: /s/ /u/ /n/ makes the word sun.
Let us try another one together. Say /d/ /o/ /g/ and push them all together.

faq.a: CVC stands for consonant vowel consonant. It means one beginning sound, one middle sound, and one ending sound.
asks: What are the three parts of the word?

faq.q: How do I know when I have blended all the sounds?
faq.a: You know you have blended when the sounds flow together smoothly into one word. It should sound like a real word.

faq.q: Do I have to say the sounds very slowly?
faq.a: At first, it is okay to say them slowly. But practice makes you say them faster until they blend easily.
asks: Is it okay to speak slowly at first?

faq.q: Can I blend words that have four sounds?
faq.a: We are learning with three sounds today. We can practice longer words later when you are ready for them.
A consonant sound is a sound made with your mouth blocking the air a little. Think of the sounds for b, m, or t.
asks: Give me an example of a consonant sound.

facts: CVC stands for consonant vowel consonant.
Blending means pushing separate sounds together.
We use sound buttons to help us say each sound.
A word like 'cat' has three distinct sounds.

quiz.why: You correctly pushed the three sounds together to make the word pig.

wrong.0: This changes the first sound from /p/ to /b/.
wrong.2: This adds an extra sound at the end which is not in the word.
wrong.3: This is just saying the sounds separately, not blending them.

quiz.say: If I say /r/ /e/ /d/, what word do I make?
quiz.why: Blending the sounds /r/, /e/, and /d/ makes the word red.

wrong.0: This changes the vowel sound in the middle of the word.
wrong.2: This changes the vowel sound in the middle of the word.
wrong.3: This adds an extra sound at the end which is not in the word.
